learn.title: Machine code, then one program
learn.body: The assembler turns assembly into machine code and saves it in an object file, ending in `.o`. An object file is not runnable yet. The linker then joins object files and library code into one program.

learn.title: Stop before linking
learn.body: The `-c` flag compiles and assembles, then stops. You get `prog.o` and no program.

learn.title: Where printf lives
learn.body: You never wrote `printf`. Its machine code sits in the C library. Your object file only says it needs `printf`, and the linker finds it and fills in the address.

learn.title: A link error
learn.body: `greet` is declared but never defined. This compiles, then the link fails with a message about an undefined symbol and the name `greet`.

learn.title: Compile error or link error?
learn.body: Match the message to the stage.
steps: `expected ';'` with a line number: the compiler
`undefined symbol` and a name, no line number: the linker
The linker works on whole files, so it has no line to point to
For a link error, check spelling and that every file is on the command line

learn.body: Compile errors give a line. Link errors give a name that has no definition.

questions.explanation: The source becomes an object file, the linker makes the program, and only then can it run.

choices: A text copy of your source
Machine code that is not yet linked
questions.explanation: An object file holds machine code with gaps the linker fills in.

questions.prompt: Which flag compiles and assembles but does not link? Type it.
The message says `undefined symbol: greet`. Which stage reported it?
questions.explanation: The compiler was happy with a declaration. The linker found no definition.

questions.prompt: Where does the machine code of `printf` come from?
choices: The C library, added by the linker
questions.explanation: The linker joins your object files with library code.

questions.prompt: The \_\_ joins object files into one program.
questions.explanation: Joining and filling in addresses is the linker's job.

questions.prompt: A link error has no line number. Why?
choices: The linker works on whole files
It is a mistake in the tool
The error is in a header
questions.explanation: By then the program text is gone, only names and machine code remain.
